body.heading: Why a twist works
paragraphs: 'Let's go for a walk' lands flat with most kids and many adults. Add a mission — find five red things, photograph the most interesting door, walk only where the dog chooses — and the same streets become a game.

The twist does two jobs: it gives everyone a shared focus, and it gives conversation somewhere easy to start. Some of the best family talks happen side by side, looking at the same thing, rather than face to face.

body.heading: Twists to try
paragraphs: Alphabet walk: spot something for each letter, in order. Photo walk: everyone takes three photos, and the best one gets shown at dinner. Grandparent-pace walk: go slowly and actually look at things — harder and better than it sounds.
Rotate who chooses the twist. The day the teenager designs the mission is usually the day they stop complaining about the walk.

description: A plain family walk gets much better with one small mission attached — here are twists that work for toddlers and teenagers alike.
